identity.title: Mapping the Release of Volatiles in the Inner Comae of Comets C/2012 F6 (Lemmon) and C/2012 S1 (ISON) Using the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array

paper_type_evidence.quote: Results are presented from the first cometary observations using the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA)

question.value: Where are HCN, HNC and H2CO released in the inner comae of comets Lemmon and ISON (nucleus vs distributed source)?

evidence.quote: present spatially-resolved measurements of the distributions of HNC, HCN and H$_2$CO within the comae of two comets originally from the Oort Cloud reservoir
Observations were made in Cycle 1 Early Science mode using the ALMA Band 7 receiver, covering frequencies between 338.6 and 364.6 GHz (0.82-0.89 mm).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two correlator settings per comet; channel spacing 244 kHz, Hanning-smoothed resolution about 0.42 km/s

evidence.quote: the channel spacing was 244 kHz, leading to a (Hanning smoothed) spectral resolution of about 0.42 km $\rm{s}^{-1}$
The spatial resolution was 0.4-0.9$''$
Comet Lemmon was observed 2013 June 1-2 and ISON was observed 2013 November 17

what.value: Gas kinetic temperature 90 K for ISON

evidence.quote: For ISON, a gas kinetic temperature $T=90$ K was adopted (cite: agu14).

what.value: Lemmon T=55 K scaled from a measurement assuming T proportional to rH^-1

evidence.quote: For Lemmon, $T=55$ K was obtained by scaling the measurement of (cite: biv13) assuming $T\propto r_H^{-1}$.

what.value: Photodestruction lifetimes of H2CO (1,280 s) and HCN (23,100 s) at 0.54 AU

evidence.quote: 1,280 s *vs.* 23,100 s for HCN at 0.54 AU; (cite: hue92)
The data were flagged, calibrated and imaged using standard routines in CASA version 4.1.0
standard routines in CASA version 4.1.0 (cite: mcm07)

flux_calibrator.value: Ceres and Titan (ISON), Pallas (Lemmon); quasars for bandpass and phase

evidence.quote: Ceres and Titan were used to calibrate ISON’s flux scale, and Pallas was used for Lemmon.
The absolute flux calibration error is expected to be less than 15%.
Deconvolution of the point-spread function (PSF) was performed using the Högbom algorithm, with natural visibility weighting and a flux threshold of twice the RMS noise in each image.
with natural visibility weighting

primary_beam_correction.value: Applied to ISON images (HPBW about 17.5 arcsec)

evidence.quote: Images of ISON were therefore corrected for the response of the ALMA primary beam (half-power beam-width $\approx17.5''$).

array_combination.value: Antennae DV07, DV19, DV24, DV25 excluded (>500 m from array centre) as no signal beyond ~400 m

evidence.quote: No signal was detected for baselines $\gtrsim400$ m, so the most distant antennae (DV07, DV19, DV24 and DV25; $>500$ m from the array center) were excluded during imaging.

final_beam.value: Gaussian fit to PSF; e.g. 0.88x0.54 to 0.54x0.40 arcsec

evidence.quote: Finally, the deconvolved images were convolved with a Gaussian fit to the PSF.

what.value: Visibility-amplitude modelling method with uniform isotropic outflow

evidence.quote: Following the method of (cite: boi07; boi14), the interferometric visibility amplitudes for the observed molecules were modeled under the assumption of uniform, isotropic outflow.
In this (cite: has57) paradigm, each molecular distribution is determined by the production rate

unstated_but_needed: Cube/channel velocity ranges for line integration
Continuum channel selection and continuum subtraction
Visibility binning and uv-range and phase centre handling in the model
Excitation model code, collision rates, and electron density
Photodissociation rates adopted for HNC and H2CO daughters
Noise treatment/fitting of real visibility amplitudes and error estimation for Lp

method.value: Standard CASA calibration; Högbom CLEAN with natural weighting, remote antennae excluded; convolved with fitted Gaussian PSF

evidence.quote: The data were flagged, calibrated and imaged using standard routines in CASA version 4.1.0

method.value: Azimuthally averaged flux in 0.05 arcsec annuli, normalised to first annulus, around HCN peak (continuum peak for continuum)

evidence.quote: The average fluxes inside successive $0.05''$-thick annuli are plotted as a function of annulus radius, normalized to unity in the first annulus.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit visibility amplitudes with Haser model

method.value: Model visibility amplitudes with Q and Lp free; least squares on real parts

evidence.quote: Goodness of fit was determined by minimizing the sum of the squares of the differences between the real parts of the observed and modeled visibility amplitudes.

key_parameters.value: v = 1.0 km/s (ISON), 0.7 km/s (Lemmon) from HCN HWHM

evidence.quote: Respective outflow velocities of $1.0$ km $\rm{s}^{-1}$ and $0.7$ km $\rm{s}^{-1}$ for ISON and Lemmon were obtained from the HWHM of the HCN lines.

assumptions.value: T=90 K (ISON), 55 K (Lemmon); excitation by H2O and electron collisions and solar IR pumping

evidence.quote: The molecular excitation calculation considers collisions with H$_2$O and electrons, and pumping by Solar infrared radiation.

fitting.value: Chi-square-like minimisation, Q and Lp free

evidence.quote: with $Q$ and $L_p$ as free parameters
The data were flagged, calibrated and imaged using standard routines in CASA version 4.1.0
For ISON, our value of $3.5\times10^{26}$ s$^{-1}$ on 2013 November 17
Our $Q({\rm HNC})/Q({\rm HCN})$ ratio of 34% is somewhat larger than the value of 18%
The $Q({\rm HNC})/Q({\rm HCN})$ ratio in comet Lemmon was only about 0.4%

findings_qualitative.value: HCN is released from or near the nucleus; HNC distributions clumpy and asymmetric, suggesting anisotropic release; H2CO has a distributed source in both comets

evidence.quote: For both comets, the dominant source of HCN was from (or very near to) the nucleus.

claims.hypothesis: Is HCN a nuclear primary species?
claims.result: HCN Lp < 50 km in both comets
claims.finding: HCN released from or near the nucleus

evidence.quote: our visibility data are most consistent with production of HCN as a primary species

claims.hypothesis: Does HNC come from a distributed or anisotropic source?
claims.result: Streams/clumps up to 1000 km in ISON; distributed source required for ISON
claims.finding: HNC released in collimated outflows from refractory material

evidence.quote: These suggest that HNC is released in collimated/anisotropic outflows.

claims.hypothesis: Does the H2CO parent scale length scale with solar flux?
claims.result: Lp a few thousand km in Lemmon, a few hundred km in ISON
claims.finding: Consistent with photolysis/thermal degradation scaling with solar flux

evidence.quote: the order-of-magnitude difference in $\Gamma$ is consistent with optically-thin photodissociation of the parent in a uniform outflow

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Excitation differences rejected as cause of HCN/HNC difference because of near-identical upper-state energies

evidence.quote: Variations in excitation cannot plausibly explain the observed differences between these molecules

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of short baselines prevents ruling out additional H2CO sources with sizes >= 5 arcsec

evidence.quote: Due to the lack of short baselines, our ALMA data cannot rule out the presence of additional H$_2$CO sources with angular sizes $\gtrsim5''$.

referee_caveats_inferred: Lemmon HNC detection is only 4.4 sigma and Lp poorly constrained
Fixed temperature and velocity assumptions; no error treatment on these

reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project codes given and CASA version known, but the visibility model code and many imaging settings are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Model code is not described in enough detail to redo the fits.

companion_papers.why: ISON non-gravitational acceleration and debris stream
